sections.h2: What are my options for a fast sale in Lower Makefield Township?
sections.html:
Sellers here can list with an agent, sell privately, or take a cash offer. Cash is the shortest path because the closing date follows your calendar instead of a buyer's mortgage approval. The township's own sale steps are light: a moving permit, a sewer lateral inspection by the seller, and clean tax and utility balances.

Bucks County homes in this part of the Delaware Valley carry high values, so even a modest delay costs real money in taxes, insurance and utilities. People who want a quick sale here usually have a reason beyond price: an estate that needs to be settled, a relocation, a divorce, a rental that has become a burden, or deferred repairs on a house that no longer fits the owner's plans.

  • Cash purchase: the buyer takes the house in its present condition and you set the closing date.
  • Agent listing: more exposure and often a higher price, with showings, repairs and a longer timeline.
  • For-sale-by-owner: you keep the commission money but handle marketing, contracts and negotiation yourself.

The township covers about 18.3 square miles in Bucks County along the Delaware River, facing New Jersey across the water. It wraps around the borough of Yardley on the north, south and west, which is why most addresses carry a Yardley mailing label even though they are in Lower Makefield. Children attend the Pennsbury School District.

About 34,028 people live here, and 87.6 percent of occupied housing is owner occupied, so most sales are single-family homes where the owner lives. The median value of an owner-occupied home was $630,200 over 2020 to 2024, median gross rent was $2,340 and median household income was $175,206 in 2024 dollars. Prices at this level make every percentage point of transfer tax and every month of carrying cost visible, so compare closing timelines as carefully as the offer price. The area sits in hardiness zone 7a, so a buyer's inspector will look at roofs, gutters and basements with winter freezes in mind.

Real estate tax comes from three bills: township, county and the Pennsbury School District. The combined 2025 rate is 256.403 mills, and the township levies no earned income tax.

2025 real estate millage on a Lower Makefield Township property

Lower Makefield Township24.95
Bucks County27.45
Pennsbury School District (2025-2026)204.003
Total256.403

One mill is one tenth of one percent of assessed value. Township and county bills are issued around March 1 for the calendar year, with a 2 percent discount for payment within two months, face amount within four months and a 10 percent penalty afterward. School bills are issued around July 1 for the school year. Unpaid taxes pass to the Bucks County Tax Claim Bureau after the collector's books close. When you sell, prorate these bills at settlement and call the tax office at 267-274-1116 for current figures.

sections.h2: What does the township require when I sell?
sections.html:
The township's community development office lists three items for a sale, and a resale use and occupancy certificate is not required in Lower Makefield Township. Confirm the current list with the office at 267-274-1100 before you schedule your closing, since a buyer's contract can add its own conditions.

  • A moving permit for both the buyer and the seller.
  • A sewer lateral inspection by the seller, to catch problems with the private line. Questions and submissions go to sewerlateral@lmt.org.
  • Calls to the taxing authorities and utility companies for any additional requirements they impose.

Allow time for a plumber to scope the line and for the township to review the report, since a failed line has to be fixed. Book the plumber as soon as you decide to sell.

Bucks County sets annual appeals by a deadline in early August. A change from an annual appeal takes effect the following tax year. Interim appeals follow the date printed on a recent assessment revision notice. The Board of Assessment Appeals meets on the first and third Tuesday of each month at the courthouse in Doylestown, and it can be reached at 215-348-6219.

Owner-occupants can also apply for the homestead and farmstead exclusion, which reduces the assessed value used for school tax. The county lists March 1 as the application deadline for the tax year that begins the following July 1. If you buy or sell an investment property, a Pennsylvania law added in 2026 asks owners to submit contact information to the Board within 30 days of a purchase, with owner-occupied homes excused.

sections.h2: Transfer tax and other closing costs
sections.html:
The state transfer tax is 1 percent of the sale value. The local share is one half of one percent to the township and one half of one percent to the school district, so the combined rate is 2 percent, split between buyer and seller by contract. Pennsylvania treats both parties as jointly responsible, so agree on who pays before signing.

Some transfers are exempt, including certain moves among family members and property passed by will or intestacy. Ask a title company to price the statement of value and recording fees at the Bucks County Recorder of Deeds, and check whether your sale involves a payoff, a lien or tenants.

sections.h2: Steps to sell in Lower Makefield
sections.html:
1. Call the township office at 267-274-1100 to confirm the current sale requirements.
  2. Hire a plumber for the sewer lateral inspection and send the report to the township.
  3. Ask the tax office at 267-274-1116 where your township, county and school bills stand.
  4. Arrange the moving permit for both buyer and seller.
  5. Have the title company prepare the statement of value and total the transfer tax.

A cash buyer skips the mortgage appraisal, but these steps stay the same. Ask who handles each one before you sign.

faqs.q: Does Lower Makefield Township require a resale certificate?
faqs.a: No. The township says a resale use and occupancy certificate is not required. It does require a moving permit for buyer and seller and a sewer lateral inspection by the seller, so call the township office to confirm.

faqs.q: What is the transfer tax in Lower Makefield?
faqs.a: The state charges 1 percent, plus a local rate of one half percent for the township and one half percent for the school district. That totals 2 percent of the sale price, divided by contract.

faqs.q: Who is responsible for the sewer lateral inspection?
faqs.a: The seller. The township expects the seller to inspect the private sewer line and submit the result, and its review can take time, so schedule the plumber early in your sale.

faqs.q: When can I appeal my Bucks County assessment?
faqs.a: Annual appeals are due in early August each year. Interim appeals follow the date on an assessment revision notice.

faqs.q: Which school district serves Lower Makefield Township?
faqs.a: Pennsbury School District serves the township, and its 2025-2026 millage of 204.003 is the largest part of the combined 256.403 mills on a Lower Makefield tax bill.
